name: vector_light_pawn_shadow_states
description: 27 phase 4 / issue #159, second half: WHICH pawns cast a lamp shadow, as against what shape it is. Vanilla refuses a pawn shadow for four reasons that have nothing to do with sunlight — not standing, psychically invisible, swimming, flying — and 27 asked none of them, so a downed colonist threw a standing-height shadow from a torch. Three colonists in one torch's reach: one upright, one anaesthetised (posture is Laying, so vanilla draws it no sun shadow either), one carrying PsychicInvisibility as a CONTROL. That third pawn is not actually invisible and is not meant to be: the hediff alone never makes a pawn invisible, because HediffComp_Invisibility only flips over when something calls BecomeInvisible(), which is the psycast's job and not the hediff's, and no number of ticks does it — CompPostTick's own write to lastBecameInvisibleTick sits inside a branch that already requires the pawn to be invisible. So the invisibility clause is verified OFFLINE, and this pawn's job here is the opposite one: to catch an implementation that suppressed on the mere presence of the hediff. It must keep both its shadows, which is why the caster pin is 2 rather than 1. The sun is deliberately up at 5.29 degrees, which makes this a test of AGREEMENT rather than of absence: the upright colonist carries a sun shadow and a lamp shadow, and the other two carry neither, so a frame where 27 disagrees with vanilla is a frame where a pawn has exactly one of the two. Swimming, flying and invisibility are covered offline only — staging them needs water plus a live job, a PawnFlyer, or a psycast, none of which a paused scenario can hold still. Posture is the clause a live capture can carry, and it is also the one an ordinary colony hits every time somebody is downed.
